title: The Unified Contraction Hypothesis & Scale-Time Calculus: A Conformal Geometric Treatise on Cosmology, Gravitation, and Fundamental Interactions
imprint_publisher: Independent Publications in Natural Philosophy and Fundamental Physics
description:
The Unified Contraction Hypothesis & Scale-Time Calculus presents a comprehensive theoretical framework, a series of 7 standalone research preprints, and an open-source Python numerical solver package (scale-cmb-solver) investigating an alternative conformal representation of cosmology and fundamental interactions. Within this framework, physical background spacetime is parameterized as a static, flat Euclidean/Minkowski continuum, while cosmological redshift, gravitational dynamics, and atomic scales originate from the secular, conformal contraction of local atomic and nuclear measurement standards (ratom(t) ∝ (1+z)-1). This work extends the conformal scale duality framework of Hoyle & Narlikar (1964) and Wetterich (2013).

📌 Core Theoretical Hypotheses

  • Static Background and Contracting Length Standards: Cosmological redshift is interpreted not as metric spatial expansion, but as the secular conformal contraction of local bound atomic standards (λ̇/λ = -H0).
  • Speed of Light and Vacuum Phase Transmission: Photons carry no translational mass displacement (vtrans = 0), propagating across the stationary vacuum as transverse elastic phase waves (vphase = c), while the internal quantum phase ceiling of bound systems is locked to this threshold (vc = c).
  • Gravitation as Vacuum Inflow: In Painlevé–Gullstrand coordinates, gravitational acceleration is formulated as the effective convective inflow velocity of the vacuum continuum into contracting matter centers (v(r) = -√(2GM/r)).
  • Sommerfeld Fine-Structure Constant: The dimensionless coupling α ≈ 1/137.036 represents the kinematic spiral pitch ratio between the tangential Bohr orbital velocity and the radial phase transmission ceiling (α = vBohr / c).
  • Effective Radial Flux Regimes: Fundamental interaction potentials are categorized by the geometric dimension (γ) of the vacuum flux: γ = 1 (3D spherical dilution: gravity and Coulomb), γ = -1 (1D collimated vortex tube: hadronic quark confinement), and γ → exponential (barrier leakage: weak interaction).

📊 Empirical Validation & Numerical Suite (scale-cmb-solver)

  • Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae: Evaluated with the official full covariance matrix without dark energy (ΩΛ ≡ 0), yielding best-fit H0 = 70.75 ± 0.14 km/s/Mpc (χ2cov/dof = 3.748 on the 26 binned sample, and χ2cov/dof = 0.945 on the unbinned N=1580 Hubble flow sample), naturally bridging the early Planck and local SH0ES Hubble tension.
  • DESI 2024 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO): The transverse comoving sound horizon ratio (c / (H0 rd) ≈ 28.81) matches all 5 DESI 2024 tracer measurements across z = 0.51 – 2.33 at < 0.85σ residual tension.
  • Planck 2018 CMB Acoustic Peaks: An analytical plasma transfer parameterization reproduces the first three acoustic peak locations (ℓ1 = 220.9, ℓ2 = 518.4, ℓ3 = 820.2), peak height ratios, and the Silk damping envelope.
  • Tolman & Goldhaber Concordance: Conformal invariance preserves Etherington's reciprocity relation (dL = (1+z)2 dA), rigorously satisfying the Tolman (1+z)-4 surface brightness dimming law and supernova light curve (1+z) time dilation.
